headline: Red Sox struggle at Fenway while the Patriots rebuild through the draft
morning_brew: Thirteen wins and twenty-one losses is a brutal way to enter the first full week of May. The Sox dropped another one at Fenway Park, falling 3-1 to the Astros in ten innings. Suarez gave us four solid innings with zero earned runs, but the bats were as quiet as the Garden after a Game 7 loss. William Contreras was the only real spark with three hits, but you cannot win games when you leave that many runners on the path. We are sitting at the bottom of the AL East, and this sub-.400 winning percentage is making my morning coffee taste like Pike water. It is a long way from the nine titles we have in the trophy case.

The NFL Draft is active and the Patriots are busy overhauling this roster in Foxborough. R1.28: Caleb Lomu, OT out of Utah. Drake Maye needed better protection all year. Love it, glaring need addressed. R2.55: Gabe Jacas, EDGE out of Illinois. The defense needs a boost on the outside. Head-scratcher, plenty of talent still on the board. R3.95: Eli Raridon, TE out of Notre Dame. We needed another target in the passing game. About time, filling an obvious gap. R5.171: Karon Prunty, CB out of Wake Forest, depth at corner. R6.196: Dametrious Crownover, OT out of Texas A&M, more protection for the pocket. R6.212: Namdi Obiazor, LB out of TCU, special teams or depth. R7.234: Behren Morton, QB out of Texas Tech, a developmental arm. R7.245: Jam Miller, RB out of Alabama, backfield depth. R7.247: Quintayvious Hutchins, EDGE out of Boston College, a local kid to round out the class.

It is a strange vibe in the Hub right now with both the Celtics and Bruins watching the playoffs from their couches. The B's have to deal with the Charlie McAvoy hearing situation, which is a massive headache for the start of next season. The league is handling the discipline for that slash, and we just have to wait for the ruling. Meanwhile, the experts are already grading the MLB start, and the Sox are not exactly acing the test. We head to Detroit next, and if this rotation does not start eating innings, it is going to be a very long summer for every townie from Revere to Quincy.

trend_watch.trend: Three hits in four at-bats against Houston.
trend_watch.dans_take: The only guy in the lineup who looks like he wants to be there right now.

trend_watch.trend: Gave up two runs and two walks in the tenth inning.
trend_watch.dans_take: Absolutely brutal way to end a close game. You have to find the zone.

trend_watch.trend: Four scoreless innings with three strikeouts as the starter.
trend_watch.dans_take: A bright spot in a dark week. He did his job, but the offense stayed on the bus.
